script:
You are a professional screenwriter.

Write a modern screenplay.

Constraints:
- No guns
- No gun violence
- No weapon combat
- No graphic violence
- No copyrighted characters
- Completely original story

Requirements:
- 10–15 scenes
- Proper screenplay format
- INT/EXT scene headers
- Dialogue in uppercase character format
- Realistic pacing

Genre: Psychological
Theme: identity

Begin screenplay.

FADE IN:

INT. LIVING ROOM - NIGHT

A room filled with darkness. Only a single lamp casts a dim light over an old, worn armchair and the book it cradles.

Suddenly, the shadows move. A figure approaches the lamp, revealing a man in his late 30s, wearing a suit and tie. JAMES. He clutches the book tightly and mutters to himself.

JAMES
(whispering)
This... this is me.

He opens the book, revealing a handwritten journal detailing his past. A tear rolls down his cheek.

INT. JAMES' APARTMENT - MORNING

James sits at his kitchen table, staring at a picture of him and his family. He looks away, then down at the paper and pen in front of him.

JAMES
(speaking to himself)
Who am I, really?

Suddenly, the doorbell rings. James looks up, unsure, then stands and walks to the door. He opens it to reveal LUCY, a woman in her late 20s with a determined look on her face.

LUCY
(excitedly)
James! I've found something!

INT. COFFEE SHOP - DAY

James and Lucy sit across from each other, a table filled with papers and documents between them.

LUCY
Your birth certificate. It was hidden away in an old, abandoned building.

James looks at the document, his eyes widening in shock.

JAMES
(shocked)
But this... this can't be right.

The document lists another man as James' father.

INT. LIBRARY - NIGHT

James sits at a table, surrounded by books about adoption and identity. His eyes scan the pages, but he can't focus.

Suddenly, a hand touches his shoulder. He jumps, startled, and turns to see RACHEL, an old friend.

RACHEL
(smiling)
Hi, James. I saw you were looking for answers.

INT. JAMES' APARTMENT - DAY

James and Rachel sit on the couch, talking about James' past and his search for identity.

RACHEL
(kindly)
James, you don't need a piece of paper to define who you are. You've always been you, no matter what that document says.

James looks at her, tears in his eyes.

JAMES
(whispering)
Thank you, Rachel. I needed to hear that.

INT. ART GALLERY - EVENING

James stands in front of a large painting, staring at his reflection in the glass. He reaches out and touches the painting, tracing the lines of his face.

Suddenly, he turns to face a woman standing behind him. It's his mother.

MOTHER
(softly)
James, I've always been proud of you.

They embrace, tears streaming down their faces.

INT. LIVING ROOM - NIGHT

James sits in the armchair, the journal open in his hands. He smiles as he reads the words he wrote long ago.

JAMES
(whispering)
This... this is me. And I'm okay with that.

FADE OUT.
